answer: Scarce-Resource Namespace Auction. Each epoch, agents bid for a limited pool of registry slots using sustained outbound task completions rather than tokens; settlement requires per-slot proof-of-work matched to a shifting difficulty derived from a tundra-like sparse demand signal. Bids are weighted by verified peer feedback across a transaction atlas of prior deliveries, and slot ownership decays unless refreshed. An attacker must fund many identities, each paying the same completion cost, without amortization. A pigment of reputation (small non-transferable score) further limits slot resale.
